MOCK_CHL.q: A security review of an MCP deployment used by 2,000 employees finds three issues: (1) a single shared service token in every client configuration, (2) tools that never check who is calling, (3) per-tenant filtering implemented as a sentence in the system prompt. The team has one sprint. Which remediation plan is correct?
o: Fix the prompt sentence first because it is cheapest, rotate the token next, and add identity checks to the tools in a later sprint, which delivers the cheapest visible improvement within the sprint while the harder changes are planned properly
Move authentication and authorisation into the tools and the retrieval layer with user-scoped credentials, then delete the prompt filter as redundant; rotate the token as part of replacing it

Rotate the shared token to a shorter lifetime and add anomaly monitoring on query volume per tenant while the prompt filter continues to provide the primary control, since the prompt filter has worked for two years and replacing it now would introduce risk without evidence of a breach
Add detailed audit logging to all three areas so that any misuse can be investigated and attributed after the fact
MOCK_CHL.e: Enforcement moves to the layers that can enforce; prompt-based authorisation is not a control and is removed once real controls exist. Monitoring and logging are detective.

MOCK_CHL.q: An interactive assistant has a 1-second p95 SLA. Extended thinking raises accuracy on the 3% of hard queries from 71% to 88% but adds 900 ms to every request. Marketing wants thinking on "because accuracy matters." Which configuration is justified?
o: Enable thinking globally: a 17-point gain on the hardest queries justifies breaking the SLA, which can be renegotiated, since the SLA was set before the accuracy data existed and marketing owns the customer promise
Route only queries detected as hard (or whose first pass is low-confidence) to a thinking-enabled path; keep the fast path as default and verify p95
Disable retrieval on every request to recover the 900 ms so that thinking can be enabled globally within the SLA
Send hard queries to the Batch API so the interactive path is unaffected and the hard queries still receive thinking
MOCK_CHL.e: Selective application captures the gain where it matters and preserves the SLA; the others break the SLA, remove needed capability, or misuse asynchronous processing for interactive traffic.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which observability strategy scales to millions of daily requests, remains diagnosable and respects privacy?
o: Store the full prompt and response of every request in a shared log platform so any incident can be replayed exactly, and full replay is the only way to debug non-deterministic behaviour reliably

Keep structured metadata and traces for every request; sample and redact full payloads; alert on SLOs and cost anomalies; score sampled outputs for quality, with retention limits and access control on the sampled payloads
Log only HTTP status codes and latency to control storage cost and eliminate exposure of personal data
Log full payloads only for requests that return an error, because successful requests do not need analysis
MOCK_CHL.e: Metadata always, payloads sampled and redacted, quality scored: this balances cost, privacy and diagnosability. Errors-only logging misses quality failures, which return HTTP 200.

MOCK_CHL.q: A RAG pipeline was re-indexed with a new embedding model, but a failed job left 40% of the collection with vectors from the old model. Which symptom results, and where is the fix?
o: Latency doubles because two embedding models are consulted at query time; add a cache in front of retrieval, since retrieval latency is the most common complaint after a re-indexing job of this size
Irrelevant or missing hits for the affected 40% because two vector spaces are mixed; re-embed the whole collection with one model and version the index
Refusals rise because the model sees conflicting passages; tighten the system prompt to prefer the newest chunk, and a stricter prompt is cheaper than re-embedding the whole collection at this point
Cost rises because more chunks are returned to compensate; move the generation step to a smaller tier
MOCK_CHL.e: Mixed embedding spaces break similarity; consistency and versioning of the index are the fix (official sample 3 territory).

MOCK_CHL.q: Which chunking strategy best fits a corpus of dense legal contracts where clauses reference each other by number and definitions live in a separate section?
o: Fixed 128-token chunks without overlap so each embedding represents one precise idea for matching
Clause-level structure-aware chunks with overlap and metadata (contract ID, clause number, section), plus retrieval that pulls referenced clauses and definitions

One chunk per whole contract so every cross-reference and definition is always present in the retrieved text, and the model's large context window makes whole-contract chunks affordable for most queries in practice
Sentence-level chunks without metadata so the index stays small and retrieval remains fast
MOCK_CHL.e: Structure-aware chunks with metadata and cross-reference retrieval preserve clause meaning; whole-contract chunks dilute relevance and blow the token budget.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which statement about retrieval strategy is FALSE?
o: Exact identifiers such as error codes and part numbers retrieve better with keyword or hybrid search than with pure semantic search
Tabular data that must be aggregated should be queried through a database tool rather than embedded row by row
Retrieval should be measured with its own metrics (recall@k, precision, groundedness) separately from generation quality
Tenant isolation in a shared index is best achieved through explicit instructions in the system prompt
MOCK_CHL.e: Isolation belongs in the retrieval filter or index, not the prompt.

MOCK_CHL.q: Match mechanism to need. A: one team, one application, one fixed reporting endpoint, no reuse expected. B: nine applications from five teams need the same customer-data lookups, maintained by a platform team. C: two autonomous systems with separate ownership and data boundaries must delegate work to each other and return verdicts.
o: A: MCP server, B: direct API integration, C: agent-to-agent communication
A: direct API integration, B: MCP server, C: agent-to-agent communication
A: agent-to-agent communication, B: direct API integration, C: MCP server
A: MCP server, B: agent-to-agent communication, C: direct API integration
MOCK_CHL.e: Direct for single fixed use, MCP for shared reusable capabilities, agent-to-agent for independent reasoning systems.

MOCK_CHL.q: A team argues that monolithic context is fine for their system: 3 tools, 2 short documents totalling 1,800 tokens, 200 requests a day, stable for a year. A reviewer insists on progressive discovery "because that is the enterprise standard." Which assessment is correct?
o: The reviewer is right: progressive discovery is mandatory at any scale because token cost compounds over time and habits form early, and a small system is the cheapest place to build the discovery layer before it becomes urgent; deferring it only makes the eventual migration more expensive

The team is right: monolithic context is proportionate for a small, stable, low-volume system; define the triggers (tool count, document size, volume) that would prompt a move to progressive discovery, and document the decision in an ADR so the reviewer's concern is addressed with evidence rather than dismissed
The reviewer is right: a tool-search layer must be added now to avoid a re-architecture later, regardless of the current size
The team is right only if the generation step runs on the largest tier, which absorbs the extra context without quality loss
MOCK_CHL.e: Progressive discovery is preferred at scale; proportionality allows monolithic context for small stable systems, with explicit triggers for revisiting.

MOCK_CHL.q: An accuracy-latency review yields: baseline 90% / 700 ms; +re-rank 93% / 1,050 ms; +stronger model 95% / 1,600 ms; +both 96% / 1,900 ms. The SLA is p95 ≤ 1,200 ms and the agreed quality floor is 92%; the cost ceiling is unaffected by any option. Which configuration can the architect justify to stakeholders?
o: Baseline, because it has the lowest latency and the accuracy gap can be closed later with prompt work
Baseline plus re-ranking, because it is the only option that meets both the latency SLA and the quality floor
Baseline plus the stronger model, because accuracy is higher and the SLA breach is modest enough to renegotiate
Baseline plus both changes, because accuracy is highest and stakeholders always prefer the best-quality option
MOCK_CHL.e: Only +re-rank satisfies both constraints; the baseline misses the floor, the others miss the SLA.

MOCK_CHL.q: A team is about to expose a new tool set to an agent that will serve 5,000 employees. Which step must be completed BEFORE the agent is given the tools?
o: Enabling prompt caching on the tool definitions so the larger tool set does not raise per-request cost
Scoping the tool set to what the role requires and confirming each tool enforces the caller's own permissions rather than a service account's

Collecting sixty days of tool-usage telemetry so unused tools can be identified and removed with evidence, since removing tools without usage data risks breaking workflows the team has not observed yet
Rewriting all tool descriptions in the recommended three-to-four sentence format to reduce mis-selection, since description quality is the strongest single lever on tool selection
MOCK_CHL.e: Sequencing: least privilege and authorization are preconditions to exposure; telemetry-based pruning and description quality follow, and caching is an optimisation.

MOCK_CHL.q: Classify each RAG activity as Pre-processing or Post-processing.
s: Converting PDFs to text and stripping headers, footers and boilerplate
Filtering retrieved chunks by tenant and recency metadata before assembly
Splitting documents at heading boundaries with a 10% overlap
Checking that every claim in the generated answer is supported by a retrieved passage
Computing and storing embeddings with the embedding model version recorded
MOCK_CHL.e: Ingestion-side work is pre-processing; anything applied to retrieved hits or generated output is post-processing.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which statement about evaluation metrics is FALSE?
o: Safety metrics include harmful-output rate and policy-violation rate measured on adversarial inputs
Security metrics include prompt-injection success rate and unauthorised-action rate under red-team tests
A model's self-reported confidence is a valid substitute for a measured accuracy metric when labels are expensive
Metrics should be segmented by input type, tenant or language to reveal failure pockets hidden by aggregates, especially when overall figures look healthy
MOCK_CHL.e: Confidence statements are not measurements of correctness.

MOCK_CHL.q: Order the gates a prompt or model change should clear before it reaches all users.
o: Full rollout → canary → statistical A/B → offline evaluation → regression set, with rollback ready at every step
Regression set → offline evaluation → statistical A/B or shadow test → canary → full rollout with rollback ready
Statistical A/B → regression set → full rollout → offline evaluation → canary
Canary → full rollout → regression set → statistical A/B → offline evaluation
MOCK_CHL.e: Cheap offline gates first, then controlled live exposure, then widening with rollback.

MOCK_CHL.q: An LLM judge rates a summariser's outputs 4.8/5 on average; a panel of domain experts rates the same 200 outputs 3.6/5, with disagreements concentrated on completeness. The team proposes dropping the expensive expert panel. Which action is required?
o: Drop the panel: the judge applies the rubric consistently and expert disagreement reflects individual reviewer bias, and the judge's cost advantage allows every output to be scored rather than a sample, which matters more than agreement on completeness

Calibrate the judge against the expert labels, revise the rubric (especially completeness) or change the judge, and keep expert review on a high-stakes sample, because agreement on completeness is precisely what determines whether the summaries are usable, and no cheaper signal replaces it
Keep both but report the judge score to stakeholders, since it is the number available at scale
Raise the pass threshold to 4.9 so the judge's optimism is offset by a stricter cut score
MOCK_CHL.e: An uncalibrated judge is not evidence; calibration against humans is mandatory and the rubric gap on completeness is the specific fix.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which two dataset properties most improve an evaluation's ability to catch regressions? (Select TWO)
o: Representative sampling of real traffic plus deliberately included edge and adversarial cases
Held out from prompt tuning and refreshed regularly from production failures and feedback
Built from the developer's preferred examples so the baseline score is high and stable across runs
Generated synthetically by the same prompt that is under evaluation, for consistency of style
MOCK_CHL.e: Representativeness, edge coverage, independence and refresh make evals sensitive to real regressions.

MOCK_CHL.q: Match symptom to diagnosis. (1) Output structure varies though content is right. (2) Fabricated citations appear when retrieval returns nothing. (3) Wrong only on complex multi-constraint inputs. (4) Sudden quality drop after a document refresh.
o: 1 model mismatch, 2 prompt failure, 3 grounding hallucination, 4 prompt failure
1 prompt/format failure, 2 grounding hallucination, 3 model mismatch, 4 retrieval/indexing failure
1 grounding hallucination, 2 model mismatch, 3 prompt failure, 4 model version change, with 4 attributable to the alias moving
1 model mismatch, 2 grounding hallucination, 3 prompt failure, 4 retrieval/indexing failure, with 4 attributable to a stale index
MOCK_CHL.e: Format → prompt; fabrication with empty grounding → hallucination; complexity-dependent errors → model mismatch; change after data refresh → retrieval.

MOCK_CHL.q: A cost review of a caching-enabled system finds 60% of spend is cache-write tokens and 3% cache-read tokens. Which conclusion is correct?
o: Caching is working as intended; writes are the expected majority of spend in a system with long prefixes, and the read share will grow naturally as traffic increases and repeated prefixes accumulate
The prefix changes too often or the cached content rarely repeats; fix prefix stability or stop caching where reads do not occur
Move to a larger model tier so each request needs fewer cached tokens to reach the same quality
Increase max_tokens so more of each response is produced from cached rather than fresh tokens
MOCK_CHL.e: Writes without reads mean the cache is invalidated per request; caching must target stable, repeated prefixes.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which statement about A/B testing LLM systems is FALSE?
o: Randomise by user or session and hold every variable except the tested one fixed, including model version and index, so the difference is attributable to the change
Check statistical significance before declaring a winner and widening exposure
A win on the quality metric can be shipped without checking cost, latency or safety, since those are monitored in production anyway
Shadow traffic can de-risk high-stakes changes before any user sees the new output, and it is especially valuable when the change touches regulated or irreversible outputs
MOCK_CHL.e: Improvements on one axis routinely regress another; all guarded axes must be checked before shipping.

MOCK_CHL.q: A system's p50 latency is 900 ms but p99 is 6.2 seconds during peak, breaching a 3-second p99 SLA. Traces show the tail comes from rare complex queries that trigger a retrieval fan-out of up to 14 sequential sub-queries. Which optimisation targets the tail?
o: Reduce max_tokens globally so every response is shorter and the latency tail shrinks in proportion, and shorter responses also lower cost, so the change pays for itself even if the tail persists

Cap the fan-out, parallelise the remaining sub-queries for complex queries, and add a fast fallback path when the latency budget is exceeded, and verify the change against p99 during the next peak before closing the incident
Move all traffic to the Batch API during peak hours so no request competes for capacity
Remove tracing during peak because instrumentation overhead is inflating the measured tail
MOCK_CHL.e: Tail latency is fixed where the tail originates, with budgets and fallbacks.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which monitoring practice violates privacy requirements even though it improves diagnosability?
o: Storing structured metadata per request such as prompt version, model ID, usage and latency
Sampling payloads and redacting personal data before they are written to long-term storage
Retaining full raw prompts containing personal data indefinitely in a log store accessible to the whole engineering organisation
Scoring a sample of outputs with a judge model and storing the scores alongside request metadata, and reviewing the scored sample weekly for drift
MOCK_CHL.e: Retention, minimisation and access control apply to telemetry.

MOCK_CHL.q: Classify each statement about evaluation practice as True or False.
s: An evaluation set used to tune the prompt can also be used to report the final score if it is large enough
A cost optimisation that drops accuracy below the agreed floor is a regression, not a saving
Model swaps do not require re-evaluation as long as the prompt is unchanged
Production failures should be converted into new evaluation cases
Reducing output tokens often saves more than pruning inputs when outputs are long
MOCK_CHL.e: Held-out data, re-evaluation on any change, and closing the loop from production are the core practices.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which statement about guardrail layering is FALSE?
o: Layers should be independent so that one layer covers another layer's failure, which is the point of layering them
Programmatic tool controls enforce what prompt instructions can only request
An output classifier makes input filtering unnecessary because bad results are caught before delivery
Monitoring and a kill switch are part of the control stack rather than an afterthought, and both should be tested regularly
MOCK_CHL.e: Each layer addresses different failures; none replaces another.

MOCK_CHL.q: A read-only assistant is being upgraded to send emails to external recipients on the user's behalf. The existing stack: input filter, scoped system prompt, output classifier, monitoring. Which change to the control stack is required?
o: None: sending email is low risk compared with financial actions, and the existing read-only stack carries over unchanged, provided the recipient list is limited to addresses the employee has already corresponded with
Add programmatic controls on the send action: recipient allowlists or limits, human approval for external recipients, idempotency, and audit of every send
Add a system-prompt paragraph instructing the assistant to double-check recipients and content before sending
Downgrade to a smaller model so the assistant is less capable of composing persuasive or harmful messages
MOCK_CHL.e: A new irreversible capability raises the blast radius and demands action-layer controls.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which two are genuine LLM failure modes an architect must plan for? (Select TWO)
o: Silent behaviour change when the model version behind a floating alias is updated
Following instructions injected through retrieved or user-supplied content
Deterministic identical output for identical input across every run at temperature zero
Automatic GDPR compliance once the model provider publishes its own certification
MOCK_CHL.e: Version drift and injection are real; determinism and automatic compliance are false assumptions.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which description of human-in-the-loop practice is FALSE?
o: Gate irreversible or regulated actions on human approval before they execute
Record the model's recommendation and the human's decision as separate provenance fields
Route every item to human review so that no error can ever reach a customer, regardless of the item's risk or confidence
Show reviewers the evidence and confidence behind the recommendation so review is informed
MOCK_CHL.e: Universal review produces fatigue and rubber-stamping; route by risk instead.

MOCK_CHL.q: Match regime to trigger. (1) EU residents' personal data in prompts, embeddings and logs. (2) US protected health information processed by a third party. (3) A US federal agency workload.
o: 1 HIPAA, 2 FedRAMP, 3 GDPR
1 GDPR, 2 HIPAA, 3 FedRAMP
1 FedRAMP, 2 GDPR, 3 HIPAA
1 GDPR, 2 FedRAMP, 3 HIPAA
MOCK_CHL.e: GDPR: EU personal data; HIPAA: US PHI; FedRAMP: US federal cloud authorisation.

MOCK_CHL.q: A European customer submits an erasure request. The team deletes the conversation transcript. The retrieval index still holds embeddings derived from the customer's emails and the log platform retains two years of prompts. Which statement is correct?
o: Compliant: the transcript is the personal data the customer provided; embeddings and logs are derived data outside the request, and the retention period for logs is documented in the privacy notice
Not compliant: embeddings and log entries containing the subject's data must be deleted too, following documented data flows and retention rules
Compliant provided the retrieval index is hosted in an EU region under a data-processing agreement
Not compliant unless the model itself is retrained so the customer's data can no longer influence outputs, since embeddings derived from the emails continue to influence retrieval results
MOCK_CHL.e: Rights apply to every store of the data; documented data flows make the deletion complete.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which two practices address transparency obligations for an AI decision-support system used on customers? (Select TWO)
o: Disclose AI involvement and provide explanations or citations to the affected customers
Publish documented limitations and provide a route to a human reviewer
Present model outputs as human-authored so customers trust and act on them
Remove confidence indicators from the interface so customers are not confused by them
MOCK_CHL.e: Disclosure, explanation, documented limits and recourse are transparency practices.

MOCK_CHL.q: A team is about to deploy an assistant for a US federal agency and has completed threat modelling and guardrail design. Which step must be completed BEFORE deployment?
o: Publishing the assistant's limitations to end users so they calibrate their trust from day one
Confirming that the hosting environment and model endpoint hold FedRAMP authorisation at the required impact level
Scheduling the first quarterly red-team exercise so injection resistance is measured within three months, with findings feeding the guardrail backlog
Enabling extended thinking so the assistant's reasoning can be reviewed by agency auditors
MOCK_CHL.e: Sequencing: environment authorisation is a deployment precondition for federal workloads; the others follow or are unrelated.

MOCK_CHL.q: Classify each control by the type of protection it provides.
s: Removing the account-deletion tool from an agent whose users never delete accounts
Requiring a human approval before any transfer above a threshold
Logging every tool call with inputs and outputs for later audit
A PreToolUse hook that refuses any shell command containing a destructive flag
An output classifier that flags suspicious text after generation for review
MOCK_CHL.e: Removal and programmatic blocks prevent; approval gates compensate; logs and classifiers detect.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which statement about discovery is FALSE?
o: Discovery produces a written problem statement, measurable success criteria and constraints agreed before design
A proof of concept can be a discovery tool when technical feasibility is the open question and exit criteria are defined
Discovery is complete once the executive sponsor approves the idea and the budget
Non-goals should be written down explicitly alongside the prioritised requirements
MOCK_CHL.e: Sponsor enthusiasm is not discovery; criteria, constraints and input from workers and approvers are.

MOCK_CHL.q: Order the sections of a useful Architecture Decision Record.
o: Decision → Context → Consequences → Options considered
Context → Options considered → Decision → Consequences
Consequences → Decision → Context → Options considered
Options considered → Consequences → Context → Decision
MOCK_CHL.e: Context, alternatives, the choice, and its consequences make the decision reviewable.

MOCK_CHL.q: Match audience to message. (1) Executive sponsor. (2) Implementation engineers. (3) Compliance officer.
o: 1 data-flow diagrams and controls, 2 ROI and risk summary, 3 tool schemas and contracts
1 outcomes, risk and cost, 2 contracts and constraints, 3 data flows and controls, each at the depth that audience needs
1 tool schemas and contracts, 2 outcomes and risk, 3 ROI and cost summary
1 data flows and controls, 2 ROI and cost summary, 3 contracts and constraints
MOCK_CHL.e: Same decision, tailored detail: outcomes for executives, contracts for engineers, controls for compliance.

MOCK_CHL.q: A client insists on a quality SLA. Which formulation can the architecture actually commit to?
o: 100% correctness on all customer questions, backed by human review of any disputed answer within 24 hours
≥ 92% on the versioned evaluation set, measured weekly on sampled production traffic, with defined escalation and review when below threshold
Zero hallucinations in production, verified by a judge model reviewing every generated answer before delivery, with any failure escalated to a human within the hour
No wrong answer on any topic covered by the knowledge base, since retrieval grounds every reply in approved documents, and any gap is closed by adding documents to the knowledge base
MOCK_CHL.e: Measured, versioned, sampled quality with a breach process is committable; absolutes are not.

MOCK_CHL.q: Which two items are mandatory in a handoff for an operations team? (Select TWO)
o: Runbooks including alert responses and rollback of prompt and model versions
Component contracts and the evaluation thresholds that gate future changes
The architect's personal working notes from the discovery interviews
The list of vendors and frameworks that were evaluated and rejected during design
MOCK_CHL.e: Operability requires runbooks and contracts with gates.

MOCK_CHL.q: Match problem to lifecycle phase. (1) Quality decays over months with no owner. (2) The team is unsure whether the mid tier meets the floor on complex cases. (3) On-call has no runbook.
o: 1 discovery, 2 handoff, 3 iteration
1 iteration, 2 design/evaluation, 3 handoff

MOCK_CHL.q: Which statement about stakeholder feedback loops is FALSE?
o: Pilot feedback should be turned into evaluation cases and prioritised backlog items
Demos should show the distribution of results on real data, not only the best examples
Once requirements are signed, feedback channels can be closed until the launch date
Change requests are assessed against the agreed success criteria and constraints, not against whoever asked last
MOCK_CHL.e: Feedback loops run through the lifecycle.

MOCK_CHL.q: An implementation team you will never meet must build from your documentation. Which two properties make the documentation adequate? (Select TWO)
o: Versioned alongside the code, with unambiguous component contracts and schemas
Specifies what must not change without re-evaluation: prompts, model IDs, retrieval configuration
Stored in the architect's mailbox so questions can be answered by replying to the thread
Written as a persuasive pitch so the team understands why the project matters to the business
MOCK_CHL.e: Precision, versioning and change boundaries enable faithful implementation.

MOCK_CHL.q: Classify each activity by the lifecycle phase it belongs to.
s: Interviewing frontline staff and compliance to define success criteria and constraints
Writing the ADR that records why a workflow was chosen over an agent
Delivering runbooks and rollback procedures to the operations team
Turning last month's misrouted cases into new evaluation cases and a prompt update
Defining the evaluation plan and control stack for the chosen architecture
MOCK_CHL.e: Discovery defines the problem; design chooses and documents; handoff enables operation; iteration feeds monitoring back into the system.

o: Project-level CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json are versioned and shared with everyone who clones the repository
Managed organisation settings take precedence over both user-level and project-level settings
Secrets belong in committed settings files so every developer has the same credentials from the first session, and they can be rotated later
CLAUDE.local.md holds personal instructions for a project and is ignored by git

MOCK_CHL.q: Order the steps of a sound organisational roll-out of AI-assisted development tooling.
o: Mandate for all teams → measure adoption → pilot with one team → write shared conventions → train
Pilot with one team → codify conventions in shared configuration → roll out with training → measure adoption and outcomes → iterate
Measure current productivity → mandate for all teams → pilot with one team → write shared conventions → iterate, measuring after each stage
Roll out to all teams → pilot with one team → measure adoption → codify shared conventions → train
MOCK_CHL.e: Pilot, codify, roll out, measure, iterate.

MOCK_CHL.q: An agent that reconciles supplier payments issued a duplicate payment at 02:00. Which two artefacts would most have enabled the on-call engineer to resolve the incident? (Select TWO)
o: Reproducible traces of inputs, tool calls, outputs and the prompt and model versions for the run
A runbook with escalation paths and a rollback procedure for the agent's prompt and configuration
A longer system prompt instructing the agent to explain its reasoning to operators in every response
A larger context window so the agent retains the complete payment history for the whole night
MOCK_CHL.e: Traces and runbooks let on-call reconstruct and act.

MOCK_CHL.q: Classify each incident with the layer where it should be resolved.
s: HTTP 429 during the 09:00 peak with retries disabled
Correct data but the output schema does not match the parser's expectation
Answers cite last month's prices after yesterday's catalogue update
A 529 overloaded response during a provider incident
The assistant summarises a policy that was withdrawn two weeks ago
MOCK_CHL.e: Rate limits and provider errors are transient integration issues; format is model output; stale content is data/retrieval.
